APC needs majority in National Assembly and House of Assembly,” he said. Reconciliation, party discipline On internal disagreements, Yilwatda acknowledged that differences and political ambitions were inevitable in a large party but said they should not be allowed to undermine its unity. Citing his political experience, he recalled losing the 2023 governorship election before subsequently serving as a minister and emerging as the APC national chairman. He urged aggrieved members to remain committed to the party, while encouraging leaders to identify dissatisfied members and create room for dialogue and reconciliation. “You may not have it today, but who told you tomorrow is same as yesterday? Work for party, stand for party. Let’s do stakeholder mapping and look at people who are aggrieved. There must be room for dialogue and conciliation,” he said. Yilwatda also warned members against undermining the party’s internal processes because their personal preferences were not reflected in the emergence of candidates. He said party members were expected to support candidates who emerged through its established procedures, regardless of individual disagreements. “Even if you don’t like him, immediately he won election, he is now my candidate. He is now party candidate. Support them because that’s what party has presented,” he said. APC chairman raises concern over polling unit agents The APC national chairman expressed concern over the delay in submitting the list of polling unit agents from Lagos State, warning that the party must avoid a repeat of the difficulties it encountered during the previous election. He directed party leaders to mobilise 10 canvassers per polling unit and ensure that the agents’ list was digitised and uploaded on time. Tinubu’s projects need better publicity On communication, Yilwatda said the APC needed to do more to publicise the achievements of the Tinubu administration, arguing that some beneficiaries of government projects were unaware of the administration responsible for them. He listed major infrastructure projects, including the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, the proposed Trans-Sahara Highway linking Calabar with northern states, the Sokoto-Badagry Super Highway, the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) gas pipeline project, and the Lagos Blue and Red rail lines. He also highlighted the administration’s tax reforms, which took effect in January 2026, saying the changes had reduced the tax burden on some low-income earners. “So many projects. People are beneficiaries, they don’t even know. Why are we silent? Tell story, sing song. Tell them what APC has done,” he said. Yilwatda maintained that the party was bigger than any individual, including Tinubu and himself, and cited the President’s participation in party screening, primary elections and other internal processes as evidence of the importance of party rules. He urged members to prioritise collective responsibility, strengthen grassroots structures and resolve internal disagreements ahead of the 2027 elections. “Road to ballot requires preparation, patience, honest communication and willingness to put collective responsibility above personal differences. “Let us build structures, strengthen relationships with grassroots, resolve differences. item.title: Adebayo condemns Plateau killings, demands urgent action
item.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja The 2027 presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Prince Adewole Adebayo, has condemned the renewed killings in Plateau State and other parts of the country, calling on Governor Caleb Mutfwang to take urgent steps to protect residents. Adebayo also criticised the Federal Government’s handling of insecurity, accusing President Bola Tinubu’s administration of failing to respond adequately to the security challenges facing the country. His position was contained in a statement issued in Abuja on Monday by Comrade Mark Adebayo, Chief Media and Communications Adviser to the Adebayo-Bugaje Presidential Campaign Council. The SDP candidate expressed grief over the killings in Plateau State, saying hundreds of people had reportedly been killed in attacks across communities between January and October 2026. He said the victims were individuals whose deaths had devastated families and communities, urging the authorities to take decisive action to prevent further loss of lives. “These are not just mere statistics; they are fathers, mothers, sons, and daughters whose lives have been violently cut short while their government stands by in criminal docility,” he said. Adebayo also criticised an earlier engagement by the Plateau State governor with residents affected by insecurity, recalling that Mutfwang had addressed traumatised citizens from inside an armoured personnel carrier. He described the incident as disrespectful to victims and their grieving families, arguing that public officials should demonstrate visible leadership and reassure communities affected by violence. “A leader cannot be hiding in an armoured tank while his people are being slaughtered daily like chickens on the very soil they call home,” he said. The SDP candidate called for an end to the killings, urging the state and federal governments to deploy available resources and security measures to protect vulnerable communities. “The time for empty press statements and crocodile tears is over. These measures use different periods and definitions and should not be treated as directly interchangeable. Why it matters : The disagreement concerns how Nigeria’s fiscal position should be measured, not simply whether public debt is increasing. Business and strategic implications : Investors need consistent fiscal reporting to assess sovereign risk. Whatever the accounting interpretation, substantial interest costs continue to constrain resources available for infrastructure and public services. The constitutional amendment remains unfinished. As of 15 October, only five state assemblies—Edo, Osun, Oyo, Rivers and Zamfara—had approved the proposed amendment, against the 24 approvals required. Meanwhile, the Presidency says a separate National Policing Bill is approximately 90 per cent ready for submission to the National Assembly. Kaduna, Plateau, Imo, Benue and other states have undertaken varying levels of preparation. These measures do not mean that state police forces have been legally established. Why it matters : Nigeria is approaching a potentially fundamental restructuring of its security architecture. Political and strategic implications: Decentralised policing could improve responses to local security threats. item.title: Passports: Nigerians in Qatar excited over improved service, honour Yakubu
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Nigerians in Qatar have honoured the Nigerian Ambassador to the country, Prof. Mahmood Yakubu, with an award for improved consular service, following the recent delivery of new passports to hundreds of them in a record time of two weeks. The presentation was made at an elaborate ceremony organised by the Nigerians in Diaspora Organisation NIDO, Qatar chapter, to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary. Hundreds of Nigerians in Qatar recently received their new passports within two weeks, a turnaround the community described as record time. Yakubu used the occasion to commend the Minister of Interior, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, and the Comptroller General of the Nigeria Immigration Service NIS, Kemi Nandap for their support. He specifically thanked them for the prompt deployment of the intervention team and the production of the passports. The event was attended by the Executive Director of the Workers Support and Insurance Fund under the Qatari Ministry of Interior, Ms Kholoud Saif Al Kubaisi, and members of the diplomatic community. item.title: Marseille’s official store looted as protests rock France
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Olympique de Marseille’s official store on the city’s La Canebière avenue was looted during weekend unrest, the Ligue 1 club said on Monday. According to Reuters, the incident came as France experienced some of its worst unrest in years, with protests over rising prices and declining public services. Thousands of people were arrested, while shops were looted or damaged. Marseille authorities imposed a ban on public gatherings and demonstrations across the city on Monday following violent protests and looting. The club condemned the attack and said it stood in solidarity with Puma, its partner that operates the store. The damage has forced the shop to close temporarily, though fans can still visit Marseille’s other official stores. Marseille said it would update supporters when conditions allow the La Canebière store to reopen. The club said in a statement: “Olympique de Marseille condemns in the strongest possible terms the acts of violence and looting targeting its official store on the Canebière and expresses its solidarity with its partner Puma, which operates the store. item.title: Rangers Petition CAF Over Disorderly Conduct Of MC Alger Fans During Champions League Match
item.description: Rangers International FC of Enugu has petitioned the Confederation of African Football (CAF) following incidents, including vandalism, involving visiting supporters of MC Alger during and after the CAF Champions League fixture at the MKO Abiola Stadium, Abeokuta, on Sunday, 18 October 2026. The club raised concerns regarding the reported destruction of a stadium entrance gate, unauthorised entry without payment of gate fees, vandalisation of stadium seats and other acts of disorder. “Rangers International FC, Enugu, confirms that it has formally petitioned the Confederation of African Football (CAF) following incidents involving visiting supporters during and after our CAF Champions League fixture against MC Alger at the MKO Abiola Stadium, Abeokuta, on Sunday, 18 October 2026,” it said in a statement posted on its X handle. Rangers have won the Nigerian title nine times. Photo: CAF Online In its petition, Rangers requested urgent intervention by CAF, including consideration of appropriate precautionary measures ahead of the return fixture scheduled for Friday, 23 October 2026, in Algiers, the capital of Algeria. “Rangers International FC remains committed to fair play, respect for football regulations and the safety of players, officials, supporters and all stakeholders,” the club stated. “We have confidence in the established processes of CAF and await its response. We thank our supporters for their continued loyalty and urge everyone to remain calm, disciplined and focused as the Club prepares for the return leg. Never Say Die.” The Enugu-based outfit beat MC Alger 2-0 in the first leg of their Champions League second preliminary round clash. The Flying Antelopes played with 10 men from the 13th minute of the clash at the MKO Abiola Sports Complex in Abeokuta, Ogun State, but scored in the 84th and 87th minutes to secure victory over their Algerian opponent. MC Alger had defeated ASN Nigelec of Niger Republic 5-0 on aggregate to qualify for the next stage. The Algerians won the domestic title and are seen as a formidable opponent for Rangers. The winner of the two-legged tie between Rangers and MC Alger will book a place in the 2026/27 group stage. item.title: JAMB warns universities against issuing admission letters
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, JAMB, has warned universities in the country against issuing admission letters to candidates seeking admission into their various institutions, insisting that such act was not within their mandate to do so. The registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, stated this when he received a delegation from Veritas University, Bwari, Abuja, which paid him a courtesy visit in his office. According to the registrar, JAMB is the only body statutorily empowered to issue official admission letters to candidates seeking entry into all tertiary institutions in Nigeria, including universities, polytechnics, and colleges of education. Prof. Aina stated that the irony of the situation is that once candidates see a document as emanating from an institution purporting to offer them admission, they believe that it is real. He, therefore, charged universities guilty of this ignoble act to desist, adding that they also have the responsibility of ensuring that those candidates obtain the right documents from the board. Furthermore, he recalled that the Federal Ministry of Education had explicitly mandated that all admissions be conducted through the Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS) and that anything done contrary to that is illegal and invalid. As a consequence, no institution is permitted to substitute its own letters for the official JAMB admission letter issued by the board after a candidate had accepted his admission on CAPS. He added that it is only admission offered through this platform is recognised and would be accepted for the purpose of mobilisation for the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), among others. item.title: Photos: COAS visits Rwanda genocide memorial, urges national unity
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, has highlighted the importance of national unity, religious tolerance and peaceful coexistence following his visit to the Kigali Genocide Memorial in Rwanda. Shaibu, who visited the memorial on Monday as part of his ongoing working visit to Rwanda, said the country’s tragic history offered important lessons on the devastating consequences of ethnic hatred, divisive rhetoric and violent extremism. The Kigali Genocide Memorial houses the remains of approximately 250,000 victims of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, serving as a solemn reminder of the dangers of unchecked hatred, political manipulation and national disunity. A statement by the Acting Director of Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said the visit underscored the need for Nigerians to rise above ethnic, religious and political differences in the collective pursuit of national peace and stability. The statement noted that Rwanda’s experience reinforced the importance of rejecting hate speech, embracing tolerance and promoting patriotism and collective responsibility among citizens. It added that the visit highlighted the critical roles of responsible leadership, early conflict prevention and sustained civil-military cooperation in preventing violent conflicts and strengthening national cohesion. The Nigerian Army chief’s visit comes amid continuing security challenges in Nigeria, reinforcing the importance of unity and collaboration in addressing threats to national peace and stability. The Army reiterated that national unity remains fundamental to achieving enduring peace, security and sustainable development. item.title: FG backtracks on recruitment waivers for varsities, clarifies approval process
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Government has clarified that federal tertiary institutions must continue to obtain recruitment waivers before employing additional personnel, amid confusion triggered by a presidential representative’s recent announcement at a university convocation. The Federal Ministry of Education, in a statement issued by its Director of Press and Public Relations, Boriowo Folasade, on Monday, said the recruitment waiver process remained in force, contrary to impressions created by remarks delivered on behalf of President Bola Tinubu at the maiden convocation of the Federal University of Health Sciences, Azare, on October 17, 2026. The clarification effectively draws a distinction between the approval of staff establishments and the authorisation to recruit, insisting that neither process has been scrapped. According to the ministry, the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation (OHCSF) retains the responsibility for approving establishment waivers, determining authorised staff strength and assessing manpower requirements across federal institutions. However, requests by tertiary institutions to recruit beyond their approved establishments are considered by a separate committee chaired by the Minister of Education. The ministry explained that the committee evaluates institutions’ staffing needs against their approved establishments before determining whether additional recruitment is justified. The OHCSF is also represented on the committee, ensuring that recruitment requests are assessed in line with approved manpower structures and existing procedures. item.description: England women’s head coach Sarina Wiegman has signed a two-year contract extension, taking her through until the end of the 2029 women’s European Championship, the Football Association announced Monday. Wiegman has led England to tournament triumphs at both the 2022 and 2025 Euros, as well as a first World Cup final in 2023, since taking charge in September 2021. item.title: Gunmen shoot Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai, three suspects held
item.description: Indian actor Tiger Shroff was shot at in Mumbai on Sunday, police said, adding that three suspects have been detained. Shooters opened fire at the 36-year-old actor as he was leaving a private event in the city’s upscale Juhu area on Sunday evening, according to Police official Mohit Garg. Aside from being India’s financial capital, Mumbai is also the heart of Bollywood, the country’s Hindi-language film industry. “Tiger Shroff is safe and Mumbai police has deployed different teams to investigate further,” Garg told reporters. Two people were injured in the incident, including the actor’s driver, though Shroff did not sustain gunshot wounds, police said. Three suspects have been rounded up in Rajasthan, another Indian state. “Preliminary questioning revealed that two of them have one case each against them, one related to theft and the other under the Arms Act,” police official Tejaswani Gautam told reporters. Police have yet to establish a motive for the shooting. Shroff is known for action films including the “Baaghi” franchise and “War”. item.title: Musk says will give SpaceX share to ‘every kid in America’
item.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said on Monday that he would give every child in the United States a share in his SpaceX rocket company. “Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America,” Musk, the richest man in the world, said on X. “This will be the first of many,” he said, without providing details about how the scheme would work. There are around 73 million children under the age of 18 in the United States, according to 2024 data from the US Census Bureau. Musk owns 38 percent of SpaceX, according to Forbes. His announcement comes after President Donald Trump promised last month to give every American adult $5,000 if his Republican party retains control of Congress in November’s midterm elections. SpaceX set the record for the largest initial public offering in history, raising $85.7 billion in June. The company’s Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the rocket central to Musk’s Mars ambitions. item.title: Bauchi: Witchcraft claim sparks violent attack as police arrest 17
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Bauchi state police command has arrested 17 suspects over an alleged witchcraft accusation that triggered a violent attack on a family in Gobirawa Village, Alkaleri Local Government Area of the state. The suspects allegedly attacked a 60-year-old man and his family after accusing the man’s son of witchcraft following the death of a 20-year-old resident, identified as Halilu Ahmad, on October 16, 2026. The incident occurred around 1am on October 18, when the suspects allegedly invaded the victim’s residence armed with machetes and sticks, inflicting multiple injuries on him and his 30-year-old son. The attackers were also alleged to have damaged two motorcycles belonging to the family. The police said preliminary investigations indicated that the attack was triggered by the suspects’ belief that the victim’s son was responsible for the death through witchcraft. Due to the deteriorating condition of the 60-year-old victim, he was initially taken to General Hospital, Alkaleri, before being referred to Ihsan Hospital, Bauchi, for further treatment. Police spokesman SP Nafiu Habib, who disclosed this in a statement on Monday, said detectives attached to Alkaleri Division arrested the 17 suspects following the incident. He said the commissioner of police, Sani-Omolori Aliyu, had directed the transfer of the case to the State Criminal Investigation Department, SCID, Bauchi, for discreet investigation and the arrest of three other suspects still at large. The police spokesman quoted the commissioner as warning against accusations of witchcraft and other unverified superstitious beliefs that could lead to violence and the unlawful punishment of innocent persons. Aliyu urged residents to report suspicions, grievances and criminal allegations to the police rather than resorting to self-help or jungle justice. He assured the public that the command would pursue justice in the case and would not tolerate actions capable of threatening public peace and security. Mourners conveying the remains of late Alhaji Shettima Muhammad Kashim after funeral prayer at the National Mosque, Abuja on Saturday He said they had been together from about 10am until shortly after 1pm at the Yar’Adua Centre, where they exchanged banter and discussed matters in their usual friendly manner. Abari said he left the group for the Friday prayer at Banex Mosque, while Kashim and the others proceeded to Maitama Juma’at Mosque, popularly known as Yar’Adua Mosque. According to him, Kashim later took his friends home after the prayers and lunch before driving towards his residence in Asokoro, where the fatal accident occurred. Abari said the news of Kashim’s death was particularly shocking because the deceased was known to be an extremely careful driver. “One thing that is distinctive about him is that he is an extremely careful, cautious driver,” Abari said, adding that the same caution characterised the way Kashim approached his responsibilities. Describing him as a person who never flaunted his privileged family background, Abari said Kashim was well brought up, good-natured and friendly to people regardless of their social standing. “He was a personification of humility, never carrying any airs around him about the kind of family he came from,” he said. Abari added that although Kashim came from a political family and held his own political views, he never allowed political differences to damage his relationships with others. The former NOA director-general said the suddenness of the death was a reminder of the uncertainty of human life. “If I recall the moments we had together, I recall the banters, everything. He looked too far away from death. But we never knew that it was just hovering around,” he said. He prayed that Allah would forgive the deceased’s shortcomings and grant his family the strength to bear the loss. ‘We were friends for almost 50 years’ Yusuf, who said he had known Kashim for almost five decades, described him as a decent, dependable and God-fearing person. In his tribute, the former NHIS executive secretary said their friendship began at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, and endured for nearly 50 years. “Arch. Shettima Mohammed Kashim and I met in ABU Zaria and have been very good friends for almost 50 years,” he said. Recounting their final hours together, Yusuf said they attended the book launch at the Yar’Adua Centre on Friday and left the venue at about 1:20pm. He said they proceeded to a mosque in Wuse II for the Friday prayer before having lunch at a nearby restaurant. They later observed the Asr prayer at the mosque before Kashim dropped him at his residence at about 4:30pm. Yusuf said he received a call from Kashim’s son about half an hour later, informing him that the family had been told that his father’s car was involved in an accident in Asokoro and that the occupant had been taken to Asokoro General Hospital. He said he rushed to the hospital, where he met members of Kashim’s family and brothers, who informed him that the architect had died. According to Yusuf, Kashim’s car ran into a stationary truck, resulting in fatal injuries. “Shettima Mohammed Kashim was more than a friend to me and many. He was a good, decent, dependable and God-fearing person,” he said. “May Allah forgive all his shortcomings and reward him with Jannatul Firdaus,” he prayed. Career as an architect Despite his family’s political background, Kashim maintained a professional career in architecture and public service, according to Abari. He said the deceased was trained as an architect and remained committed to his profession rather than using his family connections to pursue a political career. Abari recalled that Kashim served as general manager of the Borno Housing Corporation in the 1980s before moving to the federal service, where he also worked with the Federal Housing Authority. His career, Abari said, reflected a commitment to the profession in which he was trained. “He did not abandon his training as an architect,” he said. Kashim was also known by the traditional title of Shettima of Borno, a title associated with his family’s longstanding place in the traditional and political history of the region. Yusuf said the title had a historical connection to his father, Sir Kashim Ibrahim, who was conferred with the title of Shettima of Borno in 1935 and later became Waziri of Borno in 1956. Sir Kashim Ibrahim served as the first indigenous governor of the Northern Region of Nigeria from 1962 to 1966. Although his father occupied a prominent position in the country’s political history, Abari said Kashim remained approachable and maintained friendships with people of different backgrounds and political persuasions. Kashim was married to a daughter of the late Alhaji Mai Deribe, a renowned businessman.

item.title: ADAMAWA FOR ASIWAJU!
item.description: The Microphone Has Been Tested. The Signal Is Strong. The Structure Is Ready. Adamawa is ready, and its message is clear: the political structure, leadership and grassroots network are firmly in place to support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and all All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the 2027 general elections. With Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri providing leadership, direction and strategic coordination, the state is prepared to pursue a decisive victory. The commitment is firm, the objective is clear, and the target is 100% electoral victory across the board. Achieving this goal requires sustained engagement, unity of purpose and disciplined organisation. Every stakeholder, coordinator and supporter has a role to play in taking the message to the people and translating commitment into votes. At the centre of this mobilisation is the Adamawa Renewed Hope 226 Movement (ARH-226M), led by its Director-General, Professor Abdullahi Liman Tukur. It is a structured, coordinated, knowledge-driven and grassroots-focused political movement established to transform political support into organised electoral action. Its reach extends across every level of the state’s political landscape: * 4,104 Polling Units: Where every vote counts and community engagement must translate into electoral participation. * 226 Electoral Wards: Where grassroots mobilisation takes shape, relationships are strengthened and local priorities receive attention. * 21 Local Government Areas: Where leadership, coordination and stakeholder engagement connect the statewide mission with community action. Through its 21 experienced LGA coordinators, clear leadership structures and effective mobilisation strategies, ARH-226M is prepared to reach communities, engage stakeholders and consolidate support for the APC from the polling units to the state level. The task is to sustain a visible presence, listen to the people, communicate the Renewed Hope message clearly and encourage eligible voters to participate peacefully and confidently in the electoral process. From community meetings to stakeholder consultations, every engagement must strengthen trust, widen participation and reinforce a shared commitment to victory. With consistent follow-through and cooperation across party structures, the movement can keep its mobilisation focused and responsive to local realities. This coordinated effort will turn readiness into action, action into mobilisation and mobilisation into victory. Adamawa is ready. The structure is in place. The mission is achievable. One State. One Purpose. A Shared Commitment to Renewed Hope. With Fintiri as the leader, Adamawa will deliver, Insha Allah!
